root_cause.text: The nested SVM code fails to synchronize the interrupt shadow (int_state) from the hardware-updated vmcb02 to the cached vmcb12 after VMRUN of L2, causing KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE to restore stale interrupt shadow state when called after KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS, potentially hanging L2 vCPU.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "int_state is also written by the CPU, specifically bit 0 (i.e. SVM_INTERRUPT_SHADOW_MASK) for nested VMs, but it is not sync'd to cached vmcb12." The fix adds the line `svm->nested.ctl.int_state = svm->vmcb->control.int_state;` in `nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02()`.

KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit

The control state changes on every L2->L0
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 2d8a42be0e2b15a4e0b20349f27bb8288db5ebe6
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri May 22 03:50:14 2020 -0400

    KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit
    
    The control state changes on every L2->L0 vmexit, and we will have to
    serialize it in the nested state.  So keep it up to date in svm->nested.ctl
    and just copy them back to the nested VMCB in nested_svm_vmexit.
    
    Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that sync_nested_vmcb_control synchronizes event_inj, event_inj_err, and int_ctl from the hardware-updated VMCB to svm->nested.ctl, but it does not synchronize int_state (interrupt shadow). The copy of int_state in nested_svm_vmexit remains directly from vmcb->control.int_state to the nested VMCB, which does not update the cached svm->nested.ctl. Therefore, after a VMRUN, the cached int_state remains stale, and KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE will restore an incorrect interrupt shadow state, matching the described vulnerability. The committed changes do not include the necessary fix for int_state synchronization.
